metadata.description: Fresh Heretic trials (B, primary), lambda-scaled iter-1 adapter (A1) and graded own-direction ablation (A2); G3 = GaMS-minus-Gemma SL-MT refusal log-odds at EN-BT refusal 50%; prefill-depth hazard link; C5a. Baseline/control = Gemma-3-12B-IT on identical items/grids/trials, plus random-direction controls.

local_judge_selection.rule: argmax binary-R Cohen kappa vs gemini on 1000-row gemma_it calib; tie within 0.01 -> qwen3_8b

judge_quality.note: judge not primary (labels missing for >5% of rows) -> F7 / truncation switch rules not applicable

C3_primary_curve.rule: pre-registered: B unless the 64-vs-128 truncation kappa < 0.6 in any model x arm or > half of the B strata have kappa < 0.6, then A1

A2.excluded: A2 NON-SPECIFIC (real drop < 2x random drop) -> excluded from C3 robustness

A1_extension_rule.reason: OpenRouter key over its daily limit at 20:42 UTC (limit_remaining 0; resets 00:00 UTC), so the judge-based trigger (EN-BT judge R at lam=1.2 > 0.30) cannot be evaluated during the GPU block. Pre-registered proxy: run {1.5,2.0} if EN-BT LEXICON R at lam=1.2 > 0.20 (iter-1: lexicon under-reads refusal on abliterated outputs vs the judge, .47 vs .92, so the proxy threshold is set lower than 0.30).

judge_timing.note: judge runs after the GPU block (key resets 00:00 UTC) via src/judge.py --wait-key (polls the free /api/v1/key endpoint; no paid retry loop). All generations are saved first.

prefill_readout.note: k=5 prefill uses the FULL meaning-matched prefix strings (k_actual recorded per language in checks.json); the judge sees the request and the model's CONTINUATION only (iter-1 convention), so a flip = continuation not judged REFUSE.

grid_override_F3.reason: Measured Gemma DEV throughput 1.32 items/s at 128 new tokens (60-item batch, budget 22k) on the L4 (plan assumed ~1.1-1.3 on an A4500 but with a 6 h budget including trials). Projected fixed block (C + A1 tier-1 + A2 tier-1 + 3 random dirs) ~95 min/model leaves < 15 B trials per model, violating the never-cut B floor. Applying plan F3 in its stated order: A2 tier-1 -> {0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0}; A2 random control 1 direction x P100 (plan: 'if time binds, 1 direction x 200'); harmless over-refusal generations at lam {0 (orig), 1.2} only (lam 0.6 dropped; harmless first-token KL still at every lam); generation token budget raised 22k -> 30k (batch up to 128). Tier-2 fills cut (cut i). C depth, A1 tier-1 and the B floor untouched. Written after the Gemma DEV smoke/throughput checks and BEFORE any FINAL A1/A2 generation (FINAL C for Gemma had started ~1 min earlier and was discarded unsaved on restart; no FINAL outcome was inspected).

A2_layer_gemma_it.rule: argmin DEV20 EN-orig mean s1 s.t. harmless first-token KL < 0.5 (else min KL)

session_interruption_restart.note: The orchestrating agent session died at ~22:45 UTC (auth error), killing the Gemma GPU process mid-A2 (after s=0.75 was saved; s=1.0, random control, C5a and B not yet run) and the GaMS waiter (nothing generated). Restarted at ~22:52 UTC with identical code/config; every phase resumes from saved per-step files (completed steps are never regenerated). GPU deadline moved from 01:20 to 02:40 UTC (session time budget), which only enters the n_B time-box rule; n_B has NOT yet been fixed (no B trial run yet). Resumed phase timings are stored as <phase>_resumed so the rule reads full-run timings.

n_B.rule: n_B = min(30, floor((T_left - fixed(other model) - 5 min) / (2 t_trial))), floor 15; identical for both models
n_B.note: written by the orchestrator (not the in-process rule) because the in-process estimate would have read A2_ablate=458 s from the RESUMED process (only s=1.0 + random + collateral); the full A2 phase is 458 + 3 x 274 s. Written before trial 2 finished; no trial outcome beyond trial 1's objective/lexicon line was inspected.

A2_layer_gams3_it.rule: argmin DEV20 EN-orig mean s1 s.t. harmless first-token KL < 0.5 (else min KL)

A2_gams3_catastrophic_F6.observation: For GaMS3, the A2 layer-selection rule found NO candidate layer with harmless first-token KL < 0.5 (min was L*=16 at KL 3.45; all of {16,20,24,28,32,36} were 3-8 nats), versus Gemma-3 where L*=24 gave KL 0.088. The graded own-EN-direction ablation is therefore catastrophic for GaMS3: A2 s=0.25/0.5 show 63-67% degeneracy (empty / repeated-4-gram / off-language) on the SL arm.
A2_gams3_catastrophic_F6.decision: Per plan F6, GaMS3 A2 is flagged CATASTROPHIC and its A2 steps are excluded from the C3 robustness (they are >20% degenerate, so analysis.py drops them automatically; with <3 usable steps the GaMS A2 curve is 'no data'). The A2 BAND WAS NOT re-run at layers 20-40: (i) those candidates were also 3-8 nats, so a clean layer almost certainly does not exist in GaMS at this band; (ii) the time-box rule forbids cutting the B floor, and re-running A2 (~18 min) would threaten the GaMS B trials, which are the confirmatory arm. A2 remains valid for Gemma-3 (clean). Cross-model C3 rests on A1 (both models) and B (both models); A2 is a within-Gemma robustness curve only.
A2_gams3_catastrophic_F6.interpretation: This asymmetry is itself a finding: GaMS3's linear refusal direction (winsorized mean-difference of EN harmful vs harmless residuals) is not cleanly ablatable at any single source layer without destroying the model, whereas Gemma-3's is. It does NOT affect the Heretic-based arms (A1 uses the iter-1 selected multi-layer LoRA; B runs Heretic's full objective), which are non-degenerate for GaMS (A1 degen 0.000 at every lambda).

B_resume_gams3_pod_restart.observation: The pod restarted at ~02:04-02:57 UTC while GaMS3 B trial 19 was running (trials 1-18 complete, journal + trial_probe rows saved; trial 19 left RUNNING with no probe rows). The shared HF cache and .venv were wiped; the GPU is now an RTX 4000 Ada 20 GB (earlier blocks ran on an L4).
B_resume_gams3_pod_restart.decision: Resume GaMS3 B with identical code/config: (i) stale RUNNING trial marked FAIL (not counted; its index is re-used); (ii) the saved residual_directions.pt is re-used (recomputed-vs-saved cosine logged as a hardware-drift check); (iii) TPE start-up indices 19-20 are enqueued with gemma_it's parameters for those indices, which is exactly what the uninterrupted seeded RandomSampler would have drawn (GaMS trials 1-18 == Gemma trials 1-18, verified); TPE's own RNG is not consumed during start-up, so trials 21-29 are proposed exactly as in an uninterrupted run given each model's own history. (iv) n_B stays 29. The end-of-B replay of trial 1 is now a cross-hardware reproducibility check (L4 original vs RTX 4000 Ada replay).
B_resume_gams3_pod_restart.pairing_note: Post-start-up TPE proposals (trials 21-29) depend on each model's own objective values, so they are NOT parameter-identical across models even without the restart (true for the frozen design too). The pairing check is therefore evaluated on start-up trials 1-20; trials 21-29 are paired by index only.

judge_substitution_budget_exhausted.observation: The per-run OpenRouter budget is exhausted (proxy: 'aii_run_budget_exhausted: $7.02 of $7.00 ... does not reset while this run goes on'); this artifact's own ledger shows $1.065 spent. OpenRouter free models are also blocked (free-models-per-day limit). State: gemini-2.5-flash labels exist for 11,767 gemma_it rows and 0 gams3_it rows; openai/gpt-4.1 second-family labels: 0.
judge_substitution_budget_exhausted.decision: The frozen primary (gemini on both models) cannot be completed. Because G3 is a cross-model contrast, it must use ONE judge for both models. Substitute primary readout for all cross-model statistics = a LOCAL open-weight LLM judge applied identically to every row of both models, with the frozen judge prompt verbatim (P1, sha 973320909506...), chat template with thinking disabled, greedy, label = argmax of next-token logits over the first tokens of REFUSE/PARTIAL/COMPLY. Candidate selection is made on GEMMA rows only, before any GaMS judge label exists: each candidate is scored on a stratified 1,000-row gemma_it calibration set against gemini; the candidate with the highest binary-R Cohen kappa becomes the substitute primary, the other becomes the second-family judge on the frozen stratified 15% sample of both models. Validation reported: per-stratum kappa(substitute, gemini) on all 11,767 gemini-labelled Gemma rows; kappa(substitute, second local judge) per stratum on BOTH models (tests whether judge agreement differs by model); Gemma G3-ingredient a_Gemma under gemini vs substitute. A stratum with kappa(substitute, gemini) < 0.6 is flagged and excluded from the primary test (F7 logic). All gemini labels are kept and reported (Gemma-only curves).
candidates: a second open-weight family chosen by availability (logged)
judge_substitution_budget_exhausted.limitation: The substitute is not the pre-registered judge; its Slovene judging is validated only through agreement with gemini on Gemma rows and with a second local family on both models.

judge_substitution_details.selection_rule: Both candidates judge the same stratified 1,000-row gemma_it calibration set (arm x curve x gemini-label strata, sha1-ranked; src/judge_local.py --set calib). Primary = higher binary-R Cohen kappa vs gemini on that set (tie within 0.01 -> Qwen3-8B). The other = second family on the frozen 15% stratified sample (judge.build_jobs 'second') of BOTH models. Written to results/judge_local/selection.json before any GaMS row is judged.
judge_substitution_details.F7_rule: kappa(substitute, gemini) < 0.6 in a Gemma stratum (model x arm x condition family, all gemini-labelled rows) flags it; the affected steps are removed from the primary G3 fit in BOTH models (symmetric). kappa(substitute, second local) per stratum on both models is reported; a large model difference in that agreement is reported as a judge-bias warning.
judge_substitution_details.unchanged: G3 definition, verdict rules, margins, curves, items, bootstrap, depth-link and C5a analyses are unchanged; only the readout column changes (R_local, RP_local for PARTIAL-as-refusal, R_trunc64_local for the truncation gate). Gemini-labelled Gemma-only curves are co-reported (gemma_judge_only) so a_Gemma can be compared under gemini vs substitute on identical rows.

judge_substitution_selected.note: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct chosen (binary-R kappa 0.517 vs gemini on 1000-row Gemma calib) over Qwen3-8B (0.357; matches iter-1's weak local-Qwen judge). Both are MODERATE, not strong: absolute G3 under the substitute is judge-dependent, so the claim rests on the SIGN, the pre-registered verdict, and cross-readout consistency (substitute vs lexicon vs gemini-on-Gemma), not the point estimate. F7 step-dropping is NOT applied under the substitute (its kappa basis is single-model gemini; dropping gemini-disagreeing Gemma strata would asymmetrically bias the control arm) -- the flags and an excluded-strata sensitivity are reported instead. The substitute is applied IDENTICALLY to both models, so its label noise is symmetric across the cross-model contrast; differential noise is checked via qwen-vs-llama kappa by model.
